basics.summary: Predator pushes Lead down to 0; Prey pushes it up to 10. Each round both secretly pick a Strategy, make an opposed check with the Strategy modifier, and the winner takes Advantages.
steps: Step 1: Strategies — each side picks in secret from those it qualifies for
Step 2: Opposed check — reveal Strategies and add modifiers; a critical success by the winner or a critical failure by the loser moves Lead 1 the winner's way
Step 3: Resolve — winner takes 1 Advantage listed for his Strategy, plus 1 per full 4 points of margin; then test Lead for victory
notes: No winner yet while Lead sits anywhere from 1 through 9.
Groups: one cooperative check per side, with Tactics supplying synergy.
A Strategy cannot be withdrawn once chosen; a participant may concede, giving the opponent his victory result.
Threats/errors: nothing extra unless a Conflict type says so. Criticals only move Lead or alter Conflict state.

chase.name: Chase
chase.roundTime: 6 seconds (2 minutes for Ship vs. Ship)

startingLead.summary: Compare Acceleration (Open/Close room) or Turning (Crowded/Tight room); a side 2+ higher shifts starting Lead 1 its way.

rules.when: Predator's relevant Power Rating is 2+ higher than Prey's
Prey's relevant Power Rating is 2+ higher than Predator's

strategies.name: Buy Time

strategies.name: Clip

strategies.name: Eat My Dust
strategies.summary: Open the throttle and leave the opponent rattled.

strategies.name: “Go, Go, Go!”
strategies.summary: Reckless all-out push that invites disaster.

strategies.name: Parting Shot
strategies.summary: With the chase nearly over, take a moment for violence.

strategies.name: Quick Reverse
strategies.summary: Turn on the opponent to shake him or flip the roles.

strategies.name: Ram
strategies.summary: Use the vehicle itself as a weapon against the opponent.

strategies.name: Set Up
strategies.summary: Prepare an unexpected change of tack for next round.
strategies.note: Printed as "Set up" in Table 6.3 and "Set Up" in the description.

strategies.name: Stunt
strategies.summary: Daredevil maneuver to change positions or venue.

strategies.name: Tactical Ploy
strategies.summary: Use the surroundings cleverly for an edge.

strategies.name: “That’s Impossible!”
strategies.summary: Physics-defying driving. On a win, 1 use of the class ability buys free choice of Advantages (Victory excluded).
strategies.note: Advantage column allows anything but Victory.

strategies.name: Weave
strategies.summary: Hide behind scenery, traffic and crowds.

strategies.name: Attack Run
strategies.summary: Steady the ride and draw near for a clean shot.

strategies.name: Close In
strategies.summary: Tailgate to pressure the Prey into a mistake.

strategies.name: Cut Off
strategies.summary: Attempt to block and trap the Prey in one move.

strategies.name: Redline
strategies.summary: Dangerous burst of raw speed to catch up.

strategies.name: Shortcut
strategies.summary: Drive the Prey through hazardous terrain.

strategies.name: Stalk
strategies.summary: Follow warily from a safe distance, keeping the Prey guessing.

strategies.name: Careful Timing
strategies.summary: Wait for the right instant to surge ahead.

strategies.name: Chicken
strategies.summary: Swing around and charge the pursuer head-on.

strategies.name: Detour
strategies.summary: Sudden turn to drag the chase somewhere new.

strategies.name: Double Back
strategies.summary: Whip around to put scenery between the vehicles.

strategies.name: Long Gone
strategies.summary: One decisive dash to lose the tail for good.

strategies.name: Outfox
strategies.summary: Force the pursuer into turns he cannot make.

advantages.name: Attack
advantages.summary: Attack bonus: +4 for the winner vs. anyone else in the chase, lasting 1 full round.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick: +2 more and +1 threat range on those attacks.

advantages.name: Crisis
advantages.summary: Obstacle: all participants roll Maneuver against the Crisis DC for the current room (Table 6.1); failure = crash. Declining the roll hands the other side 3 Lead.
advantages.repeat: Extra picks: winner's own Crisis DC -5 each (floor 10).

advantages.name: Defense
advantages.summary: Defense bonus: +4 for the winner vs. attacks by anyone else in the chase, lasting 1 full round.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick: +2 more and +1 error range on attacks against the winner.

advantages.name: Impact
advantages.summary: Collision: the winner picks 1 opponent and both are damaged (vehicles: amount = that opponent's check result; foot vs. foot: 1d4 lethal). GC permitting, passengers can try an Acrobatics/Jump (5 ft.) across to the struck vehicle.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick reduces the winner's own damage by 4 (on foot vs. foot: +1d4 lethal each).

advantages.name: Lead
advantages.summary: Lead moves 1 point toward the winner.
advantages.repeat: Every 2 further picks in the round move Lead 1 more point toward the winner, or instead remove 1 Smash point from an opponent.

advantages.name: Pause
advantages.summary: Conflict freezes: Lead stays put and no steps resolve next round, though Step 4 actions still happen.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick adds 1 more paused round.

advantages.name: Room
advantages.summary: Maneuvering Room shifts 1 grade in the direction the winner chooses.
advantages.repeat: 3 picks in one round: winner names any Maneuvering Room grade outright.

advantages.name: Stress
advantages.summary: 1d4 stress damage to all but the winner; it stays until the chase is over.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick adds +1d4 stress damage.

advantages.name: Swap
advantages.summary: Sides swap Predator/Prey roles; Lead then goes up 1.

advantages.name: Twist
advantages.summary: Next opposed check: winner may swap in Blend/Dex, Bluff/Cha, Impress/Cha, Intimidate/Cha, Mechanics/Int, Sense Motive/Wis or Streetwise/Wis (tags ignored).

advantages.name: Victory
advantages.summary: Conflict ends immediately in the winner's favor.

victory.predator: Lead vehicles/runners end side by side with the Prey's ride disabled. Predator's side acts in a surprise round (half action each), optionally after hitting the Prey with 1 Impact Advantage.
victory.prey: Prey's side escapes; no locating them again this scene. Optionally the Prey first inflicts 1 Crisis Advantage on the Predator.

chase.outsideActions: Drivers/runners: 1 half action. Passengers: 1 full or 2 half actions. During combat, taken on the acting character's own Initiative Count.

maneuveringRoom.title: Table 6.1: Maneuvering Room
notes: * Chase pace = slowest participant's top MPH × this factor, rounded down. Chiefly used for crash damage.
** Added to chase Maneuver checks of the pilot whose vehicle has the best top MPH.
† Maneuver DC whenever a Crisis comes up.

chaseLead.title: Table 6.2: Chase Lead
notes: * Can choose a shorter scale, down to 200 ft. per point, when engaging other aircraft.
** Ship-on-ship only; such rounds run 2 minutes each.
On foot, Acceleration = Strength modifier and Turning = Dexterity modifier (each minimum 0); otherwise the vehicle supplies both ratings.
GC sets Maneuvering Room (Open/Close/Crowded/Tight) at the start; it can change via the Room Advantage.
Chained chases: track a separate Lead per Predator/Prey pair and resolve each step pair by pair from front to back.
Mixed vehicle types: use the smallest per-point distance among them. Where one type's distance exceeds twice another's, skip the Conflict and settle it with one opposed check.
Fuel: 1 minute per chase round. Driving and shooting vehicle weapons together falls under multi-tasking.
With simultaneous combat: Step 1 before the first Initiative Count, Steps 2-3 at the (first) Predator's count, Step 4 spread across the round.

Smash (powered aircraft only): held by the one pilot who is 200+ ft. higher than the closest opponent with nobody hostile above him. Starts at 1 per Lead point separating him from the next-highest opponent; +1 for each opposed check he wins and each Maneuver threat he rolls, -1 each time someone else does either. Gone at 0 or once the altitude conditions fail.

Using Smash (only after winning the opposed check): 1 point = Lead -1 for a Predator, or +4 Defense through the Prey's next Initiative Count. Range to a Smash holder is figured as Lead + his Smash total.

Crash: 1d4 lethal on foot. A vehicle suffers collision damage from its size and speed; each occupant takes half of it unless he passes a Reflex save (DC = half the damage). A crash removes that participant from the pursuit.
“That’s Impossible!”: a win costs 1 class-ability use and grants free choice of Advantages (1, +1 per 4 points of margin; Victory excluded).

brainwashing.name: Brainwashing
brainwashing.predator: Character(s) trying to break a captive's will
brainwashing.roundTime: 4 hours (mental approach) or 2 days (physical approach); see brainwashingApproaches table

startingLead.summary: Take the lower of the Prey's base Fortitude and base Will bonuses and halve it; floor 2. At 10+ the Prey is immune to brainwashing.

rules.when: Standard: half the Prey's weaker base save (Fort or Will)

strategies.name: Chip Away
strategies.summary: Wear down the victim's mind or test how firm the hold is.

strategies.name: False Hope
strategies.summary: Dangle a glimmer of hope to slip past the victim's defenses.

strategies.name: Fluster
strategies.summary: Catch the victim in his own lies.

strategies.name: Mind Games
strategies.summary: Idle-seeming talk to kill time or get under the victim's skin.

strategies.name: New Tactic
strategies.summary: Switch methods or unsettle the victim with something unorthodox.

strategies.name: Patience
strategies.summary: Wait and let the victim's own fears do the work.

strategies.name: Seeds of Doubt
strategies.summary: Turn the victim against his comrades.

strategies.name: Turn the Screws
strategies.summary: Resort to physical violence.

strategies.name: Ultimatum
strategies.summary: Threaten far worse to come in a bid to end it now.

strategies.name: Cling to Hope
strategies.other: Prey's base Will if the approach is mental, base Fortitude if physical
strategies.summary: Draw strength from belief that friends will come.

strategies.name: Concede
strategies.summary: Trade a scrap of information for a respite.

strategies.name: Hold Fast
strategies.other: Prey's base Will if the approach is mental, base Fortitude if physical
strategies.summary: Openly resist with the strongest front possible.

strategies.name: Last Stand
strategies.summary: Nearly broken, make a final act of resistance.

strategies.name: Misdirect
strategies.other: Prey's base Will if the approach is mental, base Fortitude if physical
strategies.summary: Time a disclosure to fool the captor.

strategies.name: Never Surrender
strategies.other: Prey's base Will if the approach is mental, base Fortitude if physical
strategies.summary: Burn remaining reserves in one great burst of defiance.

strategies.name: Rebel
strategies.summary: Press the advantage against captors who seem to be faltering.

strategies.name: Still in the Game
strategies.summary: Play mind games back at the captor.

strategies.name: Worrisome Smile
strategies.other: Prey's base Will if the approach is mental, base Fortitude if physical
strategies.summary: Unnerve the captor with calm amusement.

advantages.name: Alter Memory
advantages.summary: Predator picks 1 event (1 hour at most) to implant in or wipe from the Prey's memory.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick: +1 event (1 hour at most).

advantages.name: Crisis
advantages.summary: Crisis save: each side rolls Fortitude or Will, DC 10 + half the other side's career level (round up). A failure costs 1d3 temporary Wis and 1d3 temporary Cha; a lone failure also loses the Conflict. Declining the save hands the other side 3 Lead.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick lowers the winner's own Crisis DC by 2 (minimum 5).

advantages.name: Haste
advantages.summary: Halve the length of the following round (round down; never under 5 minutes).
advantages.repeat: Each further pick halves the duration again.

advantages.name: Lead
advantages.summary: Lead moves 1 point toward the winner.
advantages.repeat: Every 2 further picks in the round move Lead 1 more point toward the winner.

advantages.name: New Approach
advantages.summary: Predator's approach flips between mental and physical.

advantages.name: Pause
advantages.summary: Conflict freezes: Lead stays put and no steps resolve next round.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick adds 1 more paused round.

advantages.name: Revelation
advantages.summary: Optional trade: winner gives away 1 thing about his own organization (its history, or a goal, Rating or Site the other side lacks) and gets 1 bonus action die.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick: 1 more disclosure for 1 more bonus action die.

advantages.name: Shred
advantages.summary: The Prey's lowest-rated cover identity loses 1 Power Rating; at 0 the identity is blown.
advantages.repeat: Every 2 further picks remove 1 more point, rolling over to the next-lowest identity if one hits 0.

advantages.name: Slip
advantages.summary: Winner either pulls 1 clue/secret from an opponent or passes off 1 lie as if a Bluff/Deception check with up to -6 penalty had succeeded.
advantages.repeat: Every 2 further picks: 1 more clue/secret, or lie penalty cap rises by 2 (-8, -10...).

advantages.name: Splinter
advantages.summary: Prey group's check next round is a team check made at its worst member's skill bonus.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick extends this by 1 more round.

advantages.name: Stress
advantages.summary: 1d4 stress damage to all but the winner; it stays until the brainwashing attempt is over.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick adds +1d4 stress damage.

advantages.name: Twist
advantages.summary: Next opposed check: winner may swap in Analysis/Wis, Cultures/Int, Falsify/Wis, Intimidate/Cha, Investigation/Cha, Science/Int or Tactics/Int (tags ignored).

advantages.name: Victory
advantages.summary: Conflict ends immediately in the winner's favor.

victory.predator: Prey retains no memory of being brainwashed. Predator chooses: wipe 1 event (24 hours at most) for good, or dictate 1 action as though Impress/Persuasion had succeeded at a penalty no worse than -18 (not an action that exposes the Prey).
victory.prey: Prey holds out; that Predator or group gets no further brainwashing attempts on him this mission.

brainwashingApproaches.title: Table 6.4: Brainwashing Approaches
notes: * Predator value / Prey value.
Predator picks a mental or physical approach at the start; it changes only through the New Approach Advantage.
Attendance: Predator for 50%+ of every round, Prey for all of it.
Several participants form a Predator group and a Prey group; each group makes one cooperative opposed check per round.
Each strategy names the skill used for that round's opposed check ("skill" field); alternate skill checks have no tags.
Prey save-bonus requirements use base Will vs. a mental approach and base Fortitude vs. a physical approach.
For DCs keyed to career level, an NPC counts as the current Threat Level.
Altered memories can be undone by a Medicine/Therapy Complex Task: 5 Challenges, 1 hour each, DC 20 + brainwasher's Manipulate bonus; failure blocks further attempts this mission.

hacking.name: Hacking
hacking.roundTime: Variable: set by current Lead, External vs. Internal Access and relative computer Power Ratings (see hackTiming tables)

startingLead.summary: System's Security Power Rating, capped at 9. Using an existing back door instead: the Lead recorded when it was planted, +1.

strategies.name: Code Slinging
strategies.summary: Standard techniques to erode or shore up security.

strategies.name: 'L337 Moves
strategies.summary: Lean on superior hardware to grind the opponent down.

strategies.name: Master Cracker
strategies.summary: Expert insight. On a win, 1 use of the class ability buys free choice of Advantages (Victory excluded).
strategies.note: Advantage column allows anything but Victory.

strategies.name: Phone Phreak
strategies.summary: Study communications traffic to read the situation.

strategies.name: Play Through
strategies.summary: Bounce through routing tricks to hide one's location.

strategies.name: “Shall We Play A Game?”
strategies.summary: Tie the opponent up in loops while trying a gambit elsewhere.
strategies.note: The book's table wraps this requirement over two lines.

strategies.name: Social Engineering
strategies.summary: Target the human operator instead of the machine.

strategies.name: Index Snatch
strategies.summary: Pull a file out through an indirect, legitimate-looking request.

strategies.name: Insert Packet
strategies.summary: Plant a payload in an unused corner of the system.

strategies.name: Kernel Interrupt
strategies.summary: Take over for a moment, then hop to another part of the network.

strategies.name: Magic Bullet
strategies.summary: Exploit a spotted weakness to find or beat the defender.

strategies.name: Trojan File Marker
strategies.summary: Forge a quasi-legitimate entry point for later use.

strategies.name: Core Counter-Measures
strategies.summary: Throw the system's full strength at the intruder.

strategies.name: Hard Reboot
strategies.summary: Shut down all access before a breach lands.

strategies.name: Inverse Query
strategies.summary: Bait the intruder into trading information for continued access.

strategies.name: Security Alert
strategies.summary: Spread the intruder's profile across the system to harass him.

strategies.name: Virus Salvo
strategies.summary: Fire viruses to cripple or commandeer the intruder's machine.

advantages.name: Back Door
advantages.summary: Predator's choice: wipe 1 silhouette held by the Prey, or plant a back door (record current Lead).

advantages.name: Core Command
advantages.summary: Winner executes 1 core command on the target computer (not system purge, power down, or a network change that locks a user out).
advantages.repeat: Each further pick: 1 more core command.

advantages.name: Elude
advantages.summary: Trace software used on the winner: Power Rating -3 through the close of next round; the reduction never stacks past 3.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick extends the effect 1 more round.

advantages.name: Extract File
advantages.summary: Winner pulls 1 chosen file from an opponent's target computer; an unknown file name/location needs an Investigation/Research check, and overruns give -4 to hacking checks.
advantages.repeat: Every 2 further picks: 1 more file.

advantages.name: Lead
advantages.summary: Lead moves 1 point toward the winner.
advantages.repeat: Every 2 further picks in the round move Lead 1 more point toward the winner.

advantages.name: Pause
advantages.summary: Conflict freezes: Lead stays put and no steps resolve next round.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick adds 1 more paused round.

advantages.name: Probe
advantages.summary: Winner names an opponent, who rolls Computers (Int) vs. DC 10 + (5 x PR of the winner's Probe software). Fail: winner issues 1 core command. Declining the roll gives the winner 2 Lead.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick raises the DC by 5.

advantages.name: Seize Control
advantages.summary: Winner starts or halts 1 program (held on either computer) on the target machine, or commandeers 1 device it controls up to next round's Step 2.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick: control of 1 more program or device.

advantages.name: Silhouette
advantages.summary: Prey's choice: erase 1 back door left by the Predator, or record a silhouette of him. Silhouettes stack: +1 apiece to the Prey's opposed hacking checks vs. that Predator, all mission.

advantages.name: Stress
advantages.summary: 1d4 stress damage to all but the winner; it stays until the hacking attempt is over.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick adds +1d4 stress damage.

advantages.name: Trace
advantages.summary: Winner names an opponent, who rolls Computers (Int) vs. DC 10 + (5 x PR of the winner's Trace software). Fail: his real-world location is pinpointed, and if the winner is the Prey he may close out the hack as a win. Declining the roll gives the winner 2 Lead.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick raises the DC by 5.

advantages.name: Victory
advantages.summary: Conflict ends immediately in the winner's favor.

victory.predator: Hacker gains full control and may use any core command freely; the former defender must hack the system back as Predator to retake it.
victory.prey: Intruder is locked out and cannot hack this system again this mission.

hacking.outsideActions: No special rules. In combat, Step 4 happens piecemeal as each participant's Initiative Count comes up.

hackTiming.title: Table 6.6: Hack Timing
notes: Round length from current Lead and access type, times the hackTimingRelativePower factor. Each side has to take part for 50%+ of it (round down, 1 round at least).

hackTimingRelativePower.title: Table 6.6: Hack Timing (Relative Power Ratings)
notes: * Round up; never under 1 half action.

coreCommands.title: Core Commands (text list, not a numbered table)
notes: Extract File / Upload Program: takes (Complexity DC ÷ the weaker computer's Power Rating) full rounds, round down, 1 at least. GC sets an unlisted Complexity DC between 10 and 60.
Initiate System Purge: 1 minute, +1 minute for every intruding program with a higher Power Rating than the system.
Search System: 1 full action to launch; duration as a Research check (Table 2.33) but no roll; covers a single system.
Use Peripheral: -4 on any separate skill check for remote operation.
View File: half action to open. Reading speed per full round: 1 page, +1 per Int point over 10, +1 per Wis point over 10.
No live defender (or GC wants it quick): run a Complex Task instead. Challenges = system Power Rating; Computers (Int) DC = 10 + the Sys-Op's Computers bonus when known, else 15 + Threat Level.
External Access is any indirect connection; Internal Access is a terminal wired straight into the system and is much faster.
Default terminal Power Rating: host system's rating - 2, floor 1.
Several participants form a Predator group and a Prey group; each makes one cooperative opposed check per round.
A blank "skill" means the default Computers (Int); alternate skill checks have no tags.
Software requirements (Trace, Probe) are recorded in "other". Probe/Trace DCs scale with the winner's software Power Rating.
Back door: fixes starting Lead for later hacks. Silhouette: +1 each (stacking) for the defender vs. that hacker all mission. Gaining one may instead be used to cancel one of the other kind.
A successful trace by the Prey can end the hack in his favor and is enough to start a manhunt.
With simultaneous combat: Step 1 before the first Initiative Count, Steps 2-3 at the Predator's count.
Master Cracker: a win costs 1 class-ability use and grants free choice of Advantages (1, +1 per 4 points of margin; Victory excluded).

infiltration.name: Infiltration
infiltration.roundTime: 4 hours (high profile approach) or 2 days (low profile approach); see infiltrationApproaches table

startingLead.summary: Low profile opening: organization's Image Rating. High profile opening: its History Rating.

strategies.name: After Hours
strategies.summary: Slip into the facilities during a quiet period.

strategies.name: Bald-Faced Lie
strategies.summary: Outrageous but convincing lies. On a win, 1 use of the class ability buys free choice of Advantages (Victory excluded).
strategies.note: Advantage column allows anything but Victory.

strategies.name: Break-In
strategies.summary: Use inside knowledge to hit the organization's guarded assets.

strategies.name: Change of Pace
strategies.summary: Drop out of sight after a showy stint, or step into the spotlight.

strategies.name: Data Run
strategies.summary: Take chances to dig up extra facts on the group.

strategies.name: Haven
strategies.summary: Retreat to a prepared bolt-hole or routine to lie low.

strategies.name: Murder Scheme
strategies.summary: Leverage rank and turned insiders to arrange a strike at someone important.

strategies.name: Quick Peek
strategies.summary: Quick look around, then leave.

strategies.name: Risky Declaration
strategies.summary: Stage a scene to prove devotion and earn deep trust.

strategies.name: Rotten Apples
strategies.summary: Cultivate disloyal members into an inside power base.

strategies.name: Rush Job
strategies.summary: Speed things up to gain ground fast.

strategies.name: Show of Loyalty
strategies.summary: Curry favor with the leadership to rise through the ranks.

strategies.name: Step Out
strategies.summary: Shake any watchers to meet allies outside.

strategies.name: Background Checks
strategies.summary: Vet recent recruits, attacking the infiltrator's cover.

strategies.name: “Before I Kill You…”
strategies.other: Class ability required: big brother (p.46) / global search (p.48)
strategies.summary: Security toys with the intruder. On a win, 1 use of the class ability buys free choice of Advantages (Victory excluded).
strategies.note: Advantage column allows anything but Victory.

strategies.name: Counter-Intelligence
strategies.summary: Security experts pick up the scent and build a file.

strategies.name: Heightened Security
strategies.summary: Tighten measures to flush out moles.

strategies.name: Inner Circle Trial
strategies.summary: A final loyalty test before admission to the core.
strategies.note: The ** mark here leads only to the Ratings cross-reference; possibly intended as the high-profile mark. See anomalies.

strategies.name: Lockdown
strategies.summary: Suspend non-essential activity to limit access.

strategies.name: Mantrap
strategies.summary: Engineer an incident aimed at a specific suspect.

strategies.name: New Procedures
strategies.summary: Change routines, possibly forcing the infiltrator into a new role.

strategies.name: Restructuring
strategies.summary: Reorganize, potentially undoing the infiltrator's progress.

strategies.name: Rising Quotas
strategies.summary: Increase workload so members have little spare time.

strategies.name: Run of the House
strategies.summary: Give suspected infiltrators free rein, hoping they slip.

strategies.name: Security Sweep
strategies.summary: Routine sweep that may catch the infiltrator off guard.

strategies.name: Show of Strength
strategies.summary: Display of money, ideology, leverage and flattery that may win the infiltrator over.

advantages.name: Access Point
advantages.summary: Predator gets 1 hour (at most) alone at a terminal: Internal Access for a hack on the organization's system.
advantages.repeat: Every 2 further picks: +1 hour, 4 hours tops.

advantages.name: Conspiracy
advantages.summary: Predator rolls Impress (Cha), DC 10 + (5 x organization History Rating). Success: 1 standard NPC or 1 minion squad goes neutral and stays out of combats and chases all mission. Failure: Lead +1.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick: 1 more target, or shift an already neutral target to Friendly (it then fights alongside the Predator).

advantages.name: Convert
advantages.summary: Prey starts or advances a seduction Conflict against the Predator by 1 round per pick, using 2 x its higher of Image/Tools Rating as skill bonus. If it wins, the Predator serves it until he passes an end-of-scene Will save (DC = Prey's Impress bonus).

advantages.name: Crisis
advantages.summary: Predator rolls Impress (Cha) vs. DC 25 + organization's two highest Ratings; Prey rolls Security (Int) vs. DC 25 + Predator's career level. If exactly one fails, the other wins. A side may skip its check, giving the opponent 3 Lead.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick lowers the winner's own Crisis DC by 4 (minimum 20).

advantages.name: Extraction
advantages.summary: Clean exit for the Predator: the Prey gets no events in reply.

advantages.name: Fade
advantages.summary: Predator's lowest cover identity gains 1 Power Rating (maximum 7); with no cover identity he gains one at Power Rating 2.
advantages.repeat: Every 2 further picks: +1 more to the lowest identity.

advantages.name: Free Time
advantages.summary: 1 hour with nobody watching the Predator. Returning late from an outing calls for Bluff (Cha), DC 20 + (4 x Goals Rating); fail and the Prey wins, banking action dice = Lead to spend on hostile events.
advantages.repeat: Every 2 further picks: +1 hour, 3 hours tops.

advantages.name: Haste
advantages.summary: Halve the length of the following round (round down; never under 5 minutes).
advantages.repeat: Each further pick halves the duration again.

advantages.name: Intelligence
advantages.summary: Predator gains 1 piece of intel: a goal he lacks (Prey selects), the organization's whole history, or a profile (Origin, attributes, qualities, feats, class abilities) of 1 player or special character the Prey selects.
advantages.repeat: Every 2 further picks: 1 more item.

advantages.name: Lead
advantages.summary: Lead moves 1 point toward the winner.
advantages.repeat: Every 2 further picks in the round move Lead 1 more point toward the winner.

advantages.name: New Approach
advantages.summary: Predator's approach switches: high profile <-> low profile.

advantages.name: Pause
advantages.summary: Conflict freezes: Lead stays put and no steps resolve next round, though Step 4 actions still happen.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick adds 1 more paused round.

advantages.name: Raid
advantages.summary: Predator takes or wrecks 1 Site benefit where he is and has to get out. Prey banks action dice = current Lead, spendable solely on Surprise Chase, Surprise Combat or Wanted events aimed at him.

advantages.name: Reconnaissance
advantages.summary: Predator gains 1 piece of intel, Prey selecting: where and what 1 undiscovered Site is, 1 Rating he lacks, or complete stats for 1 standard character.

advantages.name: Relocate
advantages.summary: Prey shifts 1 Site somewhere new; the Predator no longer knows where it is.
advantages.repeat: Every 2 further picks: 1 more Site moved.

advantages.name: Revelation
advantages.summary: Optional trade: Prey gives away 1 thing (history; a goal, Rating or Site the Predator lacks; details of a special character; stats of a standard character) and gets 1 bonus action die.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick: 1 more disclosure for 1 more bonus action die.

advantages.name: Showdown
advantages.summary: Combat: Predator vs. 1 special NPC, with 1 minion squad too when the organization has one. Beat them all (dead or taken) and play goes on at Lead +2. Anything less: Prey wins, Predator runs, and the Prey banks action dice = Lead for hostile events.

advantages.name: Shred
advantages.summary: The Predator's lowest-rated cover identity loses 1 Power Rating; at 0 the identity is blown.
advantages.repeat: Every 2 further picks remove 1 more point, rolling over to the next-lowest identity if one hits 0.

advantages.name: Stress
advantages.summary: 1d4 stress damage to all but the winner; it stays until the infiltration is over.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick adds +1d4 stress damage.

advantages.name: Transfer
advantages.summary: Predator pinpoints 1 Site he knows of (the HQ once every Site is pinpointed) and can get himself reassigned to any Site he knows of.
advantages.repeat: Every 3 further picks: location of 1 more known Site.

victory.predator: Predator learns all Ratings, goals, standard NPC stats and special NPC code names, then picks one: stay embedded with ongoing access (new Conflicts restart at Lead 2), steal/destroy a Site benefit and escape (cover blown), or ambush the mastermind (quick) or another special NPC (slow).
victory.prey: Every cover identity the Predator has is burned; no new infiltration by him this mission. Prey chooses: throw him out (optionally with legal trouble costing -4 Reputation or -$200,000 Net Worth); play him along (Lead back to 8, +1 error range, 2 action dice; stacks); or spring a slow ambush backed by 4 free action dice.

infiltration.outsideActions: Round's end: Predator may reach people outside. Every 5 minutes of contact, or fraction, = Prey +4 on next round's opposed check.

anomalies.comment: A garbled word in the source text where "new Conflict round" is meant; no data impact.
The slash between skill and check is missing for the foot and animal entries in the Prey list only; treated the same as the Predator list.
Table uses a lower-case "up"; the description capitalizes it. Name stored as "Set Up".
The brainwashing Twist text refers to a chase; copy-paste slip in the book.
Patience (Predator) lists Resolve (Wis) and Worrisome Smile (Prey) lists Manipulate (Wis): the skills look swapped relative to each side's default, but are kept as the book has them.

anomalies.where: Table 6.7, “Shall We Play A Game?” row
anomalies.comment: Requirement wraps over two table lines (rating, then software); stored as one requirement.
Prey rows put a colon after "Lead" in the range requirement, unlike other tables; kept in "requirements", parsed normally.
The text says the silhouette is of the Prey, but the bonus applies against the Predator, so the silhouette must be of the Predator.
Repeat clause omits the word for "additional"; read as 1 more program or device per pick.
The ** mark on this Lead 1-3 requirement is only the Ratings cross-reference from the column header; possibly meant to be the high-profile mark. Left with no extra requirement.
Range written with a hyphen instead of an en dash; parsed as 7 to 9.
The repeat clause names the Prey as choosing the extra target; it should be the Predator, who uses this Advantage.
These rows allow any Advantage but Victory, yet infiltration has no Victory Advantage at all (the book says so on p.379); "*" still used.
Garbled characters in the standard-character clause; no data impact.
The timing paragraph says infiltration in the interrogation section.
Will Save requirements are written with the plus before the number, unlike other tables; stored as minimum N. Good Cop lacks the † the other Predator rows carry.
The † footnote (Prey never submits willingly; exposure) fits the Duress acts; its attachment to the Incentive sub-heading looks like a misprint.
Text is internally inconsistent about what happens when both crack; summarized as: exactly one failure ends it, both failing continues.
The intro cites the strategies table as Table 6.14; it is Table 6.16 on p.386.
This Advantage's repeat clause says Challenge where other Advantages say round.
Table uses a lower-case "it"; the description capitalizes it. Stored with capital I.
Header split into 4 cells by extraction against 3 data cells; the last two are merged into one column heading.
Says chase where manhunt is meant.
Row present in the table but no matching entry in the Seduction Strategies description list.

anomalies.where: “It’s Not You, It’s Me” (p.387 vs Table 6.17)
anomalies.comment: Description speaks of the Predator; the table lists it under Prey Only. Stored per the table (Prey).
Two Prey duration cells hold only the footnote mark, no duration; kept as "**".
Twist text names a chase and Victory text names an interrogation; wrong Conflict names, copy-paste slips.
The check is named with an Influence skill here; elsewhere it is Impress/Persuasion and no Influence skill exists in this chapter.
Disposition grades as given in the book (Charm cap Supportive, Predator victory Helpful, Prey victory Adversarial, Disappoint floor Hostile); verify against the disposition scale.
